title: Universal coefficient comparison for closed-test models
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and on every small pro-etale site put $\Lambda_Y=p_Y^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use internal $\Lambda_Y$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], their exact inverse images and ordinary unbounded derived direct images computed on K-injectives [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. All sites and section values are taken in a common sufficiently large universe. Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak a\subseteq A$ an ideal, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $s:Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak a)\hookrightarrow U$. Let $v$ be the affine ind-etale closed-site lift [def-exc-closed-site-lift]. Let $V\to Z$ be an affine ind-etale object such that $V$ and $B=v(V)$ are w-contractible [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. Let $f:X\to U$ be a morphism of affine schemes and put $X_Z=X\times_UZ$, with projections $h:X_Z\to X$, $f_Z:X_Z\to Z$. Put $T=X\times_UB$, $T_0=X\times_UV$ and $a:T_0\hookrightarrow T$; products mean scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $c:\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a morphism of commutative condensed rings and write $\operatorname{Res}_Y$ for exact restriction of scalars on module sheaves and their ordinary derived categories [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. For any scheme morphism $b:Y'\to Y$, let
$$\delta_b:\operatorname{Res}_Y Rb_{*,\Lambda'}\longrightarrow Rb_{*,\Lambda}\operatorname{Res}_{Y'}$$
be the right-derived comparison induced by the ordinary sectionwise identity $b_{*,\Lambda}\operatorname{Res}_{Y'}=\operatorname{Res}_Yb_{*,\Lambda'}$. For any object $W$ of the site of $Y$, similarly let
$$\gamma_W:R\Gamma_{\Lambda'}(W,-)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{\Lambda}(W,\operatorname{Res}_Y(-))$$
be the comparison induced by the identity on ordinary underlying abelian section groups; its direction and normalization are those of the universal right-derived units [def-sfb-right-derived-functor].
The comparisons $\delta_b,\gamma_W$ commute with site localization, the actual closed-test unit-section maps $F(B)\to(s^*F)(V)$, the ordinary pullback composition maps, and the unit–counit mate for the square. Consequently the squares comparing the normalized closed-test section models $Q(\mathcal I(T))$, $Q(\mathcal J(T_0))$ for the two coefficient systems commute, as does the square for their chain restriction $Q(j(T_0)\circ\eta_a)$. Here $\mathcal I$ represents a bounded-below object and $\mathcal J$ resolves its $h^*$-pullback; the section models are identified with derived sections by the actual closed-unit inverse and degreewise localization identities. These equalities are equalities in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$, and are natural for every actual derived module map $K\to\operatorname{Res}_XN$, with $K$ bounded below over $\Lambda_X$ and $N$ bounded below over $\Lambda'_X$. They apply in particular to $M[0]\to\operatorname{Res}_X(\Lambda'_X\otimes_{\Lambda_X}M)[0]$ induced by the ordinary scalar-extension unit $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. No derived tensor unit is substituted for this map. No preservation of K-injectives by $\operatorname{Res}$ and no invertibility of $\delta_b$ or $\gamma_W$ is assumed or asserted.

The statement, stmt_deps and blueprint field are identical to the Q27 re-split version. The live node is still unsplit and there is no repair note, so the delivery is not superseded. There are no new nodes and no SGA. Step 2: I checked the types of the exact-square lemma (U=r_{Y'}, V=r_Y, F=b_{*,S}, G=b_{*,R}; for sections V=id). This gives δ_b: Res Rb_{*,Λ'}→Rb_{*,Λ}Res and γ_W in the item's direction, with uniqueness, and Res is not assumed to preserve K-injectives. Step 3: ring-sheaf-change d has the same direction and the same computation-unit normalization, so d=δ_b. The adjunct identity with t=id and t=ε^S gives exactly the two displayed unit and counit equations. Step 5: I re-derived δ·r(Ex')=Ex_{rN}·s^*δ_f by naturality of δ, the unit/counit substitution, the θ square and naturality of η; it is genuinely elementary. Steps 4 and 6–8: the localization squares come from the degreewise identity (09T5 uniqueness plus slice-localization). The unit-section inverse commutes with restriction because underlying sections do not change. The pasting with chain-mate gives γ_{T0}r_S=r_R γ_T, and the cospans use only forward γ arrows; the D^+ naturality comes from localized-model-coherence plus K-injective Hom. Step 9 uses the ordinary unit m↦1⊗m. Edge cases checked: c=id, 𝔞=0, 𝔞=A, Λ'=0, and non-flat ℤ→ℤ/2, where restriction loses K-injectivity and the proof re-resolves. Batch-5 findings: lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization is a generic internal/section normalization cited by 14 sfb nodes, and neither assumption gives it; lem-trf-localization-essentially-surjective is a pure category-theory Mathlib leaf.
